record.title: U.S. and China establish a Super Intelligence dialogue and incident channel; operating details remain undisclosed
record.summary: The White House (September 25), China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (September 26), and China’s Ministry of Commerce (September 28) each published official accounts of a new bilateral advanced-AI dialogue and an incident communication channel. The White House calls it the U.S.-China Super Intelligence (SI) Dialogue and an SI-incident channel; the Chinese accounts call it an AI dialogue and an AI-incident channel. Both governments say another exchange is due by November 2026. MOFCOM places the dialogue within the U.S.-China economic and trade consultation mechanism and says Vice Premier He Lifeng and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent are the lead officials and that an initial exchange already occurred during the September talks. These are government statements of agreed diplomatic arrangements. The inspected announcements do not identify contact points, an incident threshold, activation procedures, response timelines, information-sharing rules, a legal instrument, or evidence that an operational channel has been tested.
organizations: Government of the People’s Republic of China
Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The White House and China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs independently state that the two governments agreed to establish a bilateral communication channel for advanced-AI incidents and a dialogue on risks and benefits.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: MOFCOM says that, within the U.S.-China economic and trade consultation mechanism, Deputy Premier He Lifeng and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent lead the dialogue; an initial exchange occurred during the September talks, and the next dialogue will be held by the end of November 2026.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The inspected official announcements do not specify named operational contact points, incident thresholds, activation or response procedures, or an information-sharing protocol; therefore the channel’s practical operation and effectiveness remain unknown.

evidence_gaps.description: Public sources do not name responsible operational contacts or define the incident threshold, activation process, response timeline, information-sharing safeguards, or status of a staffed channel.

brief.importance_rationale: A formal bilateral dialogue and incident-communication commitment between the two largest AI powers could change crisis communication and cross-border AI-risk governance. The score stays at 6 because the public announcements provide no operating protocol, assigned contact points, incident threshold, legal obligations, or evidence of tested use.
limitations: The governments use different public terms: the White House says “Super Intelligence” and SI incidents; Chinese MOFCOM and MFA say artificial intelligence and AI incidents. This record preserves that wording rather than assuming an agreed incident definition.

No public operating protocol, contact list, qualifying-event threshold, response time, information-sharing scope, technical channel, formal treaty or tested case was found in the inspected statements.
Official statements establish announced government positions and claimed agreement, not that a standing or staffed channel is operational.
MOFCOM reports an initial exchange during the September talks; the White House and MFA material inspected here mention the next dialogue but do not independently detail that initial exchange.
The public documents do not establish whether lab reporting, model-release safeguards, export controls or private-sector duties are within scope.

technical.claimed_result: MOFCOM reports that He Lifeng and Scott Bessent lead the dialogue and an initial exchange occurred. These statements establish what the ministry reports, not the channel’s readiness or effectiveness.
technical.compute_or_cost: Not applicable to this diplomatic mechanism.
technical.demonstrated_result: The governments published matching commitments to create the dialogue/channel. The White House describes the dialogue as established with an exchange due by November; the Chinese MFA records bilateral agreement; MOFCOM additionally reports a first exchange. No operational use was observed in the inspected sources.
technical.implementation_status: Announced commitment; operational implementation, contact points and procedures not publicly specified in the sources inspected.
technical.mechanism: Government-to-government dialogue held within the U.S.-China economic and trade consultation mechanism, paired with a bilateral incident-communication channel, according to MOFCOM. Public descriptions leave the channel’s operating design unspecified.
technical.regime: Diplomatic arrangements announced in official summit outcome statements, September 25–28, 2026.
technical.strongest_baseline: Before the September summit, a September 4 Reuters report described talks as planned and agenda/participants as fluid. The September 25–28 official accounts now confirm that the two governments agreed to a dialogue/channel, but do not validate every earlier reported agenda detail.

brief.title: U.S. and China establish a Super Intelligence dialogue and incident channel; operating details remain undisclosed
brief.why_it_matters: An announced incident-communication mechanism between the two largest AI powers could provide a route to reduce misinterpretation and escalation around cross-border AI events. It is a material change in bilateral AI-risk diplomacy, while its practical value remains unknown until each side publishes operating responsibilities and procedures and demonstrates use. The announcement itself does not establish a binding safety standard, common incident taxonomy, lab-reporting duty, or technical safeguard.
